records.sourceFile: The influence of injury history on countermovement jump performance and movement strategy in professional soccer players - Implications for prof.pdf

sourceVerification.doiVerification: DOI printed in the local PDF text.

records.evidenceSummary: Cross-sectional comparison of 20 full-time professional outfield players at one English Championship club: 10 had a previous lower-limb injury that kept them out of training for at least 3 months, and 10 had none. Double-leg jump height and flight time to contraction time ratio did not differ between groups, but single-leg jumps did, with the previously injured group jumping lower and producing less eccentric and concentric force, including in the uninjured limb.
records.limitations: Ten players per group from one club, with no pre-injury baseline and no classification of injury type, so the group differences cannot be attributed to the injury. Single-leg analysis pooled both limbs of each player as if independent, and the Table 3 r-squared values for the non-injured group conflict with the text: the text gives 44% for jump height and 89% for time ratio, but Table 3 places 0.89 against jump height and 0.44 against time ratio, and its time-ratio second step (0.44) is lower than its first (0.78).
records.synthesisCaution: Staff may treat single-leg jump deficits as a validated return-to-play test or as proof of injury-caused weakness, when this is a small group comparison that cannot show whether a given player is ready or at risk.

changes: screeningLimitations: Table 3 r-squared description made precise. The text gives 44% for jump height and 89% for time ratio (noninjured group); Table 3 lists 0.89 against jump height and 0.44 against time ratio, and its time-ratio step 2 (0.44) is below step 1 (0.78).
paper.limitations: 'the Table 3 values do not match the text' -> 'the noninjured values in Table 3 (0.89 for jump height, 0.44 for time ratio) are reversed relative to the text (44% and 89%)'.

Confirmed without change: identity and full title, DOI 10.1123/jsr.2020-0243 (printed page 1), 2021;30(5):768-773 (JSR Vol. 30, No. 5 printed), 3 authors, 10 vs 10 with injured defined as out of team training 3 months or more, 20 full-time outfield players at an English Championship club, 5 trials per limb, double-leg null results, single-leg p = 0.007 (jump height) and p = 0.005 (time ratio), depth 22.29 vs 16.68 cm (Table 2), injured-group Table 3 values (75%, 84%, 70%, 89%).
verification.residualConcerns: Table 3 noninjured row labels and r-squared values disagree with the text and with a stepwise reading; the text values are used. A reviewer should check the original Table 3 layout before relying on the noninjured R-squared figures.
